paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The difference between probing a single layer and probing the weighted sum of layers. concat is the concatenation of all layers. 0 is the embedding layer. Large negative values on the y-axis mean that probing the particular layer on the x-axis is much worse than probing the weighted sum of all layers.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the difference in performance, measured as a percentage point difference, between probing a single layer and probing a weighted sum of layers for two models, mBERT and XLM-R. The horizontal axis, labeled “layer,” lists integers from 0 to 12, followed by "concat," representing the embedding layer and the concatenation of all layers respectively; these categories are arranged in ascending numerical order. The vertical axis, labeled “% point difference,” represents a linear scale ranging from -10 to 0, with tick labels at -2, -4, -6, -8, and -10. The upper chart displays data for the mBERT model, with light blue bars showing values ranging from approximately -1.5 for layer 11 to approximately -9.5 for layer 1, with values generally decreasing from layers 0 to 2, then remaining broadly consistent before rising for layer 11. The lower chart shows data for the XLM-R model, with dark blue bars representing values from approximately -1.5 for layer 1 to approximately -9 for layer 4. The bars in this chart decrease in height from layers 0 to 4, then rise slightly to layer 6. No bars are visually emphasized, and the charts are not sorted by any apparent attribute.
